content: Short Norwegian rhetorical questions that question authenticity (e.g., "Eller bedrar skinnet?") should be classified as negative sentiment, as they imply deception.
Identify sentiment-bearing adjectives (e.g., "skinnende") and evaluate their polarity.
Recognize contextual cues that imply benefit (e.g., "hides cables" for cleaner appearance) as positive signals.
Do not default to negative when no overt adjectives; consider implied positive features.
Assuming absence of explicit evaluative adjectives equates to negative sentiment.
Ignoring contextual implications that turn a neutral description into a favorable one.
When encountering a word that may carry sentiment in the source language, perform a quick translation to English (or the target language) to confirm its polarity before applying sentiment rules.
Assuming that nouns or non‑adjective tokens are neutral; many nouns in the source language (e.g., "God" in Norwegian) are sentiment words and should be treated as such.
